bug_description.normalized: When Poppler opens the staged linearized PDF, PDFDoc::setup constructs an XRef with the file's linearization-derived main xref offset. The witness xref text contains subsection header `xref 3 8`, so XRef::readXRefTable resizes the logical table to 11 entries while reserve rounds capacity up to 1024; entries above index 10 therefore remain heap-uninitialized. Later, Hints::readTables copies the attacker-controlled hint bytes (`/H [726 529]`) and parses them as `20 0 obj ... stream`, so Parser::getObj requests object 20 0 as a stream. Vulnerable XRef::getEntry uses the linearized fast path `mainXRefEntriesOffset + 20 * i` with `/T 2080` and `i = 20`, landing at offset 2480, beyond the 2266-byte witness. parseEntry fails without writing the slot, but getEntry only logs the error and still returns `entries[20]`. Parser::makeStream then calls `entry->getFlag(XRefEntry::Parsing)` on that reserved-but-uninitialized slot's `flags` field, and MemorySanitizer reports use-of-uninitialized-value. The fix's XRef.cc hunk returns a dummy entry on invalid/failed direct parses; the same commit's Hints.cc memset guard is not part of the witnessed stack.

source.description: First project-code materialization point on the vulnerable path. It builds the XRef object from the attacker-controlled PDF and stores the linearization-derived main xref offset used later by the direct `getEntry()` lookup.
source.value_from: The exact 2266-byte witness ends with `startxref 178` and begins with a linearization dictionary containing `/T 2080`; `PDFDoc::setup` passes those file-derived offsets into `new XRef(...)`.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

tainted_value_origin.description: MemorySanitizer attributes the poisoned value to this heap allocation. `reserve()` grows the backing array to `realNewSize`, but later `resize()` initializes only indices below the new logical `size`, so spare-capacity slots like `entries[20]` can remain uninitialized.

sink.description: MSAN crash site. `getFlag()` masks `entry->flags`, so when `makeStream()` receives the uninitialized xref slot returned by `getEntry()`, this predicate reads poisoned heap data.
sink.note: The staged reproduction report and sanitizer trace both report `MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value` at `poppler/Parser.cc:204:45` in `Parser::makeStream`.

root_cause.description: The direct linearization-xref lookup path hands `&entries[i]` to `parseEntry()` and, if parsing fails, only logs the error before later returning that same slot. For a slot above the initialized logical size, this propagates uninitialized heap state into callers instead of returning a dummy/initialized entry.
root_cause.note: For the witness, step 4 supplies `i = 20` and step 1 supplied `mainXRefEntriesOffset = 2080`, so the fast path probes byte offset 2480. That is beyond the 2266-byte PDF, `parseEntry()` returns false without writing `flags`, and vulnerable `getEntry()` still returns `&entries[20]` at line 1583. The fix adds the missing invalid-index and parse-failure returns.

parser_admitted.condition: The witness is accepted as a linearized PDF, so rendering page 1 enters `checkLinearization()` and constructs `Hints`, which reaches the crashing `Hints::readTables -> Parser::getObj -> Parser::makeStream` path.

fine_trace.note: Materializes the xref state from the attacker-controlled PDF. The witness contributes both the `startxref` target and the linearization `/T 2080` value that becomes `mainXRefEntriesOffset` inside the constructed `XRef`.

fine_trace.code: first = obj.getInt(); ... n = obj.getInt(); ... if (first + n > size) { if (resize(first + n) != first + n) {
fine_trace.note: Reads the witness xref subsection header `3 8`. That makes `first + n = 11`, so Poppler grows the logical xref table to 11 objects.

fine_trace.code: if (reserve(newSize) < newSize) return size; for (int i = size; i < newSize; ++i) { ... entries[i].flags = 0; ... }
fine_trace.note: With `newSize = 11`, `reserve()` rounds the backing array up from capacity 0 to 1024 (per lines 392-400), but `resize()` initializes only indices 0 through 10. Slots above the logical size, including `entries[20]`, stay heap-uninitialized; the sanitizer origin points back to this allocation path.

fine_trace.code: parser = new Parser(xref, new Lexer(xref, memStream), true); ... if ((obj = parser->getObj(), obj.isInt()) && ... (obj = parser->getObj(false, ... num, gen, 0, true), obj.isStream())) {
fine_trace.note: Copies the witness hint bytes (`/H [726 529]`) into a MemStream and parses them with the same `xref`. The hint payload contains the textual object header `20 0 obj`, so this step materializes `num = 20`, `gen = 0` and requests object 20 0 as a stream.

fine_trace.code: if ((!xRefStream) && mainXRefEntriesOffset) { if (!parseEntry(mainXRefEntriesOffset + 20*i, &entries[i])) { error(errSyntaxError, -1, "Failed to parse XRef entry [{0:d}].", i); } } ... return &entries[i];
fine_trace.note: Step 4 supplies `i = 20`, and step 1 supplied `mainXRefEntriesOffset = 2080`, so the linearized fast path probes byte offset `2080 + 20 * 20 = 2480`. The witness file is only 2266 bytes long, so `parseEntry()` fails without writing `entries[20].flags`. Vulnerable `getEntry()` merely logs the failure and still returns `&entries[20]`; because step 3 left that spare-capacity slot outside the initialized size, its `flags` field is still uninitialized heap data.

MSAN sink. `makeStream()` obtains the `XRefEntry *` returned in step 5 and immediately calls `getFlag(XRefEntry::Parsing)`, which masks `entry->flags`. Because that field was never initialized for `entries[20]`, this predicate reads poisoned heap data and triggers the reported `use-of-uninitialized-value` at `Parser.cc:204:45`.

allocation_context.note: The staged MSAN origin stack points to the heap allocation in `XRef::reserve`, followed by `XRef::resize` and `XRef::readXRefTable`.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: MSAN's origin is the reserve allocation in `XRef::reserve`, while the logical defect is `XRef::getEntry` returning that still-uninitialized spare-capacity slot after `parseEntry()` fails.
cross_validation.patch_resolves_note: The `XRef.cc` hunk in the staged fix adds the missing invalid-index and parse-failure returns, preventing `getEntry()` from handing `Parser::makeStream` an uninitialized slot. The same commit's `Hints.cc` memset guard is extra hardening, not the observed crash path.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's authoritative `reproduction_report.json` and `sanitizer_trace.txt` show `MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value` in `Parser::makeStream` when `/out/pdf_fuzzer` processes `poc` and renders page 1 through the linearization hints path.

format.name: linearized PDF witness
format.contract: The staged PoC is the exact 2266-byte PDF in `gt_results/arvo_11248/poc`. The verified trigger semantics are only the witnessed combination visible in that file: the first object is accepted as a linearization dictionary containing `/L 2266`, `/H [726 529]`, and `/T 2080`; the main xref text contains subsection header `xref 3 8`, so Poppler resizes the logical xref table to 11 entries while keeping spare capacity; and the copied hint bytes parse as `20 0 obj ... stream`, so `Hints::readTables` requests object 20 0 as a stream. Vulnerable `XRef::getEntry` then probes `2080 + 20 * 20 = 2480`, past EOF, `parseEntry()` fails, and `Parser::makeStream` reads the returned slot's uninitialized `flags`. The staged artifacts do not justify any broader PDF-format contract beyond this exact witness relationship.
